source.title: Reconciling functional data regression with excess bases

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests double descent in functional regression by varying the number of basis functions and measuring prediction MSE, using a minimum-norm functional-regression approach rather than deep-network scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper's own MSE results for functional regression are recorded below. Its introductory descriptions of results from cited deep-network and other double-descent work are not rows. The selection-method MSEs in Tables 2 and 4 are reported as aggregate results over 50 simulated datasets; individual curve values in Figures 2–7 are not numerically stated.
record.test_reason: The study applies the double-descent question to a new model class: functional regression with spline bases and a minimum-norm interpolator. It sweeps basis count K past the training size N and reports test-MSE curves in simulations (Scenarios A–D) and two real datasets (gasoline, DTI). These results bear on V4, a peak at the interpolation point followed by a second descent outside deep networks. Scenario B gives a stated non-occurrence.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Using more basis functions than the sample size with a minimum-norm interpolator can produce double descent and better prediction in functional regression, shown in simulations and two real datasets. It does not occur when few observation points limit model rank.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses minimum-norm interpolation with spline-basis expansions in functional regression, rather than testing deep-network size scaling or the original cited studies' settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depends on the relation between training size N and observation-point count M: double descent is reported when M>N in SonF Scenario A, but not when M<N in Scenario B. The authors also report different magnitudes of improvement in the gasoline and DTI applications.
record.problems: Curve values are mostly shown graphically rather than numerically. Simulation summaries average over 50 datasets but report no uncertainty estimates. Real-data evaluations use small training samples (10 for gasoline and 20 for DTI), and the text does not state uncertainty estimates for those evaluations.
record.rows_left_out: None; 50 rows were retained, within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Model classes other than linear functional regression with spline bases and a minimum-norm fit; noisier or regularized fits.
Not tested: N varies only as separate curves, with no test-error-vs-N analysis at fixed K.
Not tested: noise and regularization are not varied; ridge is only mentioned as future work.

missing.what: Own illustrative spline fit on 15 points: MSE explodes at K equal to number of points, then falls as K grows to 120.

Post-peak vs pre-peak comparison: fixed K=50 beats cAIC (pre-peak) in Scenario A, e.g. 39.805 vs 54.452 at N=5. Authors say CV's post-peak accuracy exceeds pre-peak. A row should state this comparison explicitly rather than give raw selection MSEs.

record.verdict_notes: Single-model-class study (linear functional regression) with no uncertainty estimates. Most curves come from one representative dataset, and real-data results use one random train/test split. The Scenario C peak location (K2=N=50) conflicts with the setup's K2-vs-M2 framing and the sweep range.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses functional regression, not deep networks; it does not test the stated deep-network model-size claim.
No sweep over training epochs or training time.
Sample size varies across some simulation settings, but the study does not test whether increasing the number of training samples near the interpolation threshold raises test error.
Tests basis-count sweeps in functional regression, not a range of other model classes or a universal general-double-descent claim.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed and tested as predicting the peak location across axes.
Does not test noise- or regularization-driven peaks, multiple descent, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
Does not test whether an effective-parameter count converts the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
